chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Hadeed from Murazim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sick person who is unable to perform the prayer. He said, 'Whenever God overcomes him [with weakness], God is more deserving of the excuse.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a sick person who is too weak to pray?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this narration to clarify the threshold of incapacity in the chapter of the *Mudtirr* (one compelled by necessity), emphasizing that divine excuse applies when weakness becomes overwhelming. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that *al-ghalabah* (dominance of the condition) relieves the individual from the strict obligation of *salat*, reflecting the mercy inherent in divine law. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how physical limitations are weighed against ritual duties in Shia fiqh.
